name: Kiro
license: Proprietary (AWS-operated product surfaces; IDE based on Code OSS with Open VSX extensions)

runner.notes: Install Kiro IDE and/or CLI, authenticate (GitHub/Google/AWS Builder ID or IAM Identity Center), open only runs/<run-id>/worktree, provide prompt.md via chat or CLI, optionally use specs/sub-agents, then harness-verify. Record surface (IDE/CLI/web), plan tier, model, and interventions. Prefer local IDE/CLI over web sandboxes for Class A parity.

inclusion: Direct Class A agentic software development environment: AWS-built IDE, CLI, web, mobile, and Crew surfaces sharing one agent harness for specs, parallel sub-agents, hooks, MCP, and PR delivery.
pricing_model: Credit-based: Free (50 credits), Pro $20, Pro+ $40, Pro Max $100, Power $200 per user/month; team plans with SSO via IAM Identity Center; add-on credits at $0.04/credit. Enterprise sales available.
public_stack_signals: Official site: agentic IDE, CLI, and web interface for prototype-to-production engineering.
IDE is Code OSS-based with Open VSX extensions and VS Code settings import.
Unified agent harness across IDE, CLI, Web, Mobile, and Crew with shared .kiro/ configuration.
Spec-driven development: requirements, design, sequenced tasks, property-based tests, parallel agents.
Built and operated by AWS with IAM/SSO, governance, and enterprise admin controls.
capabilities_to_probe: CLI headless mode and CI/CD automation
hooks, steering, skills, powers, and MCP tools
web sandboxed multi-repo sessions and PR flow
ACP compatibility for bringing Kiro agent into other tools
moat_hypotheses: AWS distribution, compliance, and enterprise identity stack
spec-driven agent harness as a structured alternative to pure vibe coding
one harness spanning IDE, CLI, web sandboxes, mobile, and Crew
credit packaging with predictable overage vs opaque rate limits
setup_notes: Download IDE/CLI from kiro.dev/downloads; CLI install via curl https://cli.kiro.dev/install.
AWS account is not required for individual social/Builder ID login.
Web autonomous mode and cloud sandboxes are not parity-equivalent to local IDE/CLI runs.
Credit exhaustion mid-task is a major parity risk; record plan tier and remaining credits.

research.positioning: An AWS-operated agentic development environment that turns prompts into specs and shipping code across IDE, CLI, web sandboxes, mobile, and Crew, with enterprise identity and credit-based packaging.

runtime: web agent sessions in cloud sandboxes
frontend: web app for delegated multi-repo work
backend: unified agent harness shared across surfaces
AWS-operated model inference and account services
enterprise IAM Identity Center / governance plane
packaging: desktop installers per OS via downloads page
data: cloud sandbox workspace state for web mode
unknowns: Closed-source implementation details of the harness and sandbox runtime are not published as a full source tree.
Git worktree isolation semantics for parallel local agents need hands-on confirmation before parity claims with worktree-first peers.

infrastructure: Local IDE and CLI run on the developer's machine against the project checkout.
Web mode runs agent sessions in isolated cloud sandboxes and can coordinate GitHub/GitLab changes.
Enterprise deployments use AWS identity, governance, and regional controls documented under enterprise docs.
Model traffic uses Kiro-hosted or plan-available models; BYO third-party harnesses like OpenClaw are prohibited per pricing FAQ.

agent_support: ACP-compatible embedding of the Kiro agent
orchestration: hooks on file save / tool use / task completion
workspace_isolation: web sandboxes for isolated cloud sessions
local multi-agent isolation model not fully specified in reviewed docs
review_shipping: checkpoints and rewind for agent changes
property-based tests for correctness against specs
remote_mobile: Kiro on the web for remote delegated work
context_memory: MCP and Powers for external context
integrations: Figma, Terraform, and other Powers catalog entries

parity_risks: Credit limits and model multipliers change capacity mid-run.
Web sandbox runs are not parity-equivalent to local IDE/CLI.
Spec mode vs vibe chat mode changes intervention and planning cost.
Enterprise SSO tenants may see different model/region availability.

hypotheses: AWS trust, identity, and enterprise procurement accelerate team adoption.
Spec-driven workflow differentiates from pure multi-CLI cockpits.
evidence: Official docs describe one harness powering every surface via .kiro/.
Homepage and enterprise pages state AWS operation, IAM/SSO, and governance.
Published credit pricing with free tier and team plans.
unknowns: Comparative single-task code quality vs Claude Code/Codex alone is unmeasured here.
Depth of local multi-agent isolation relative to worktree-first ADE peers needs hands-on runs.
